audit.title: Getting Started with Chainlink CCIP

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The page opens on "Available Blockchain Families" rather than a one-line answer to its own title. A lifted top chunk explains chain support before it ever defines CCIP or what "getting started" entails.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong — 4 clean headings, 1 H1, 0 level skips, tight bulleted sections all under 51 words. Ideal chunk boundaries for RAG. No action needed beyond content depth.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 3 numerals, none with units, no version strings, no fees, latency, finality times, or count of supported chains. "Ethereum, Avalanche, Polygon, and other EVM-compatible networks" is illustrative but unquantified.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 5 links, all internal, 0 to primary sources. No link to the CCIP whitepaper, architecture spec, or a canonical concept definition.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: No verbatim-liftable definition of CCIP anywhere on the page — the single largest missed opportunity for a getting-started entry point.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: No JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no `dateModified` in head (only a body-text "Last Updated: 2025-05-19"), no og/twitter tags. Head metadata could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>`.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code blocks. Acceptable for a routing hub that delegates to platform guides; not penalized as a defect, scored neutral.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers "what can I build" and "which chains" and routes by platform, but omits "what is CCIP," pricing/fees, and any troubleshooting/FAQ entry point.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent "CCIP" / product naming, unambiguous prose, clean lists.

audit.summary: This is a short (179-word) navigation hub routing developers to platform-specific CCIP getting-started guides (EVM, SVM, Aptos). Its biggest strength is clean, well-chunked structure with consistent terminology; its biggest weakness is that it never states what CCIP *is* — there is no quotable, self-contained definition an engine can lift when answering "what is Chainlink CCIP." As a hub page it does its routing job, but as a retrieval target it forfeits the highest-value query ("what is CCIP / how do I start") and carries no schema, canonical URL, or authoritative external references. The honest verdict: functional index page, underbuilt for generative retrieval.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical CCIP definition as the first liftable sentence
recommendations.where: immediately under the H1, before "Available Blockchain Families"
recommendations.issue: page jumps to "CCIP supports multiple blockchain families" with no definition.
recommendations.change: add 1–2 sentences, e.g. "Chainlink CCIP (Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol) is a cross-chain messaging and token-transfer protocol that lets smart contracts send data, tokens, or both between blockchains. This guide routes you to platform-specific setup for EVM, SVM (Solana), and Aptos."
recommendations.why: gives engines a self-contained definition to cite for "what is CCIP" — the dominant entry query this page currently can't win.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics near the chain list
recommendations.issue: "and other EVM-compatible networks" — no counts or specifics.
recommendations.change: state the number of supported networks/lanes (e.g. "CCIP supports N+ networks; see the CCIP Directory") and name the CCIP token standard/pattern. Quantify wherever the Directory allows.
recommendations.why: quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation; "other networks" is unquotable.

recommendations.title: Add a "How do I get started with CCIP?" and symptom-phrased framing
recommendations.change: phrase the section lead as the user question ("How do I get started with CCIP?") and add one line each on when to pick EVM vs SVM vs Aptos so an engine can extract a *reason* for the choice.
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by task; question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept titles lose.

recommendations.title: Emit JSON-LD `TechArticle` + canonical URL + dateModified
recommendations.issue: canonical MISSING, 0 JSON-LD blocks, dates only in body text.
recommendations.change: add `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `dateModified` (mirror the 2025-05-19 body value), canonical URL, and `inLanguage`.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and visible freshness raise agent trust/parseability (E-E-A-T).

recommendations.title: Add one authoritative outbound reference
recommendations.change: link the CCIP architecture/spec or whitepaper as the canonical source for the protocol definition.
recommendations.why: inline primary-source links raise credibility and citation rate.

antiPatterns: Freshness signal ("Last Updated: 2025-05-19") lives in body text only, not machine-readable head metadata.
No undated/stale content, no keyword stuffing, no fluff, no unresolved cross-references — prose is clean.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced from the page — good site-level signal; ensure it lists this hub and its three child guides.
Canonical URL, JSON-LD, and og/twitter tags are template/site-level fixes, not authorable in body content.
The `.md` endpoint strips `<head>`; pass raw HTML head to the CLI to confirm whether schema/canonical exist on the rendered page before treating them as absent.
